title: Mirrored Min-of-K Training
abstract: arXiv:2611.29008v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Min-of-K (MoK) training is widely used to train models that produce diverse outputs from random noise. For each target, it draws K outputs from the model and backpropagates only through the one closest to the target. However, MoK generally does not make the generated distribution match the data distribution. In this paper, we analyze the MoK bias across all values of K and show that tuning K shifts between failure modes, from mode dropping at small K to distribution flattening at large K. We further prove that every nontrivial loss based only on target-candidate distances fails to recover some data distribution, since these distances do not reveal how the candidates are placed relative to each other. Based on these analyses, we propose mirrored MoK (MMoK), a drop-in modification of MoK training that draws one extra sample from the model, applies the closest-candidate selection rule against it, and subtracts the resulting distance. translated_abstract: K选一训练被广泛用于训练能从随机噪声中生成多样化输出的模型。对于每个目标，该方法从模型中采样K个输出，并且仅对最接近目标的那一个进行反向传播。然而，MoK通常无法使生成分布与数据分布相匹配。本文分析了MoK在所有K值下的偏差，并表明调整K值会在不同的失败模式之间切换：K较小时出现模式丢失，K较大时出现分布平坦化。我们进一步证明，任何仅基于目标-候选距离的非平凡损失都无法恢复某些数据分布，因为这些距离无法反映候选样本之间彼此的相对位置关系。基于这些分析，我们提出了镜像K选一训练，这是一种可直接替换MoK训练的改进方法，它从模型中额外采样一个样本，针对该样本应用最近候选选择规则，并减去由此得到的距离。由于……
tldr: 该论文提出镜像K选一训练（MMoK），通过额外采样一个样本并减去其最近候选距离来纠正MoK训练的分布偏差，并证明仅基于目标-候选距离的损失函数必然无法匹配某些数据分布。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes Mirrored Min-of-K (MMoK) training, a drop-in fix that corrects MoK's distribution bias by drawing an extra sample and subtracting its closest-candidate distance, while proving that any loss based solely on target-candidate distances fails to recover some data distributions.
